{

    "test:all": "pnpm run test && pnpm run test:deno && pnpm run test:bun",
    "check": "vp check",
    "check:fix": "vp check --fix",
    "lint": "vp lint src runtime-tests build perf-measures benchmarks adapters",
    "lint:fix": "vp lint --fix src runtime-tests build perf-measures benchmarks adapters",
    "format": "vp fmt --check \"src/**/*.{js,ts,tsx}\" \"runtime-tests/**/*.{js,ts,tsx}\" \"build/**/*.{js,ts,tsx}\" \"perf-measures/**/*.{js,ts,tsx}\" \"benchmarks/**/*.{js,ts,tsx}\" \"adapters/**/*.{js,ts,tsx}\"",
    "format:fix": "vp fmt \"src/**/*.{js,ts,tsx}\" \"runtime-tests/**/*.{js,ts,tsx}\" \"build/**/*.{js,ts,tsx}\" \"perf-measures/**/*.{js,ts,tsx}\" \"benchmarks/**/*.{js,ts,tsx}\" \"adapters/**/*.{js,ts,tsx}\"",

    "watch": "pnpm run remove-dist && vp pack --watch && pnpm run copy:package.cjs.json",
    "coverage": "vp test --run --coverage",

    "release": "np --no-publish",
    "remove-dist": "rm -rf dist",
    "build:adapters": "pnpm -r --filter \"./adapters/*\" run build",
    "test:adapters": "pnpm -r --filter \"./adapters/*\" run test",

      "types": "./dist/types/request.d.ts",
      "import": "./dist/request.js",
      "require": "./dist/cjs/request.js"
    },

Done. Implemented `trustIncoming?: boolean` on the requestId middleware with tests, and verified.

## Changes

**`src/middleware/request-id/request-id.ts`**
- `RequestIdOptions` gains `trustIncoming?: boolean` (`request-id.ts:16`)
- Destructured with `trustIncoming = true` — default preserves existing behavior (`request-id.ts:46`)
- Header read is now gated: `trustIncoming && headerName ? c.req.header(headerName) : undefined` (`request-id.ts:52`). When `false`, the incoming header is never read, so the existing fallback path always calls `generator(c)`; `c.set('requestId', reqId)` and `c.header(headerName, reqId)` are unchanged, so the generated value is still exposed both ways.
- JSDoc documents the new option (`request-id.ts:26`)

**`src/middleware/request-id/index.test.ts`**
- New `describe('Request ID Middleware with trustIncoming option')` block with 5 tests: default trusts header, explicit `true` trusts header, `false` ignores a valid incoming header (UUID in both `c.get('requestId')` and response header), `false` always uses a custom generator, and `false` generates when no header is sent.

## Verification

```

→ Test Files  1 passed (1)
  Tests       16 passed (16)
```

`pnpm exec tsc -p tsconfig.spec.json` also exits 0.

All changes are unstaged, per the git-safety contract — nothing was added or committed.
